description: Imagine biting into a soft, airy Focaccia Genovese, its golden crust glistening with fragrant olive oil and speckled with fresh rosemary. This iconic Italian flatbread, originating from Genoa, is a testament to simple ingredients creating extraordinary flavor. Perfect as an appetizer, side, or even for sandwiches, its irresistible texture and savory aroma will transport you straight to the Ligurian coast.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until a foamy layer appears on the surface, indicating the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Mix the Dough
instructions.text: Add the all-purpose flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy, cohesive dough forms. Drizzle in 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil and continue mixing until it is fully incorporated into the dough.

instructions.title: First Rise (Bulk Fermentation)
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl. Transfer the dough to the oiled bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a damp kitchen towel. Let the dough rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until it has visibly doubled in size.

instructions.title: Prepare the Pan and Dimple
instructions.text: Generously drizzle about 2-3 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil into a 9x13 inch baking pan, ensuring the bottom and sides are well coated. Gently transfer the risen dough to the pan, turning it over to coat both sides with the oil. Using your fingertips, gently stretch and dimple the dough to evenly spread it across the pan.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Flavoring
instructions.text: Cover the pan again with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let the dough rise for another 30-45 minutes. While it rises, preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). After the second rise, create deeper dimples with your fingers, then generously drizzle with more olive oil, sprinkle with fresh rosemary and flaky sea salt.

instructions.title: Bake the Focaccia
instructions.text: Place the pan in the preheated oven and bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and cooked through. The bottom should also have a nice golden color.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the focaccia from the oven and let it cool in the pan for a few minutes. Carefully transfer it to a wire rack to cool completely, or serve warm. For an extra touch, drizzle with a little more fresh extra virgin olive oil before slicing and enjoying.

tips: For the most authentic flavor, always use a high-quality extra virgin olive oil, especially for the final drizzle. It truly elevates the taste.
Do not overwork the dough; focaccia thrives on a gentle touch to maintain its airy, open crumb. The dimpling process should be light and swift.
Focaccia is best enjoyed fresh from the oven on the day it is baked. If you have leftovers, a quick toast in a pan or oven will revive its crust and warmth.
article:
The scent of freshly baked bread, infused with aromatic herbs and golden olive oil, is one of life's simplest yet most profound pleasures. Among the vast repertoire of Italian baking, Focaccia Genovese stands out – a true culinary masterpiece hailing from the Ligurian coast. This isn't just any bread; it's a testament to simplicity, quality ingredients, and a rich culinary tradition. When elevated with the fragrant notes of rosemary and the richness of good olive oil, it transforms into an irresistible Rosemary Focaccia that captures the essence of Italy in every bite.

Imagine a bread that's crisp on the outside, incredibly soft and airy within, riddled with inviting dimples, and glistening with a generous slick of extra virgin olive oil. That's Focaccia Genovese. It's more than just a side dish; it's an experience, a journey to the sun-drenched streets of Genoa, where this iconic flatbread reigns supreme. This article will guide you through understanding, baking, and savoring this authentic Italian delight, ensuring your homemade Rosemary Focaccia is nothing short of spectacular.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?

Focaccia Genovese, or *Fügassa* in the local Ligurian dialect, is the quintessential flatbread from Genoa, the capital of Italy's Liguria region. Unlike its thicker, more rustic cousins found elsewhere in Italy, the Genovese version is characteristically thin, incredibly tender, and boasts an open, airy crumb. Its signature features include a deeply dimpled surface, which acts as tiny wells for the abundant extra virgin olive oil and coarse sea salt that generously adorn its top.

Historically, focaccia in Liguria served as a breakfast item, often dipped in coffee or milk, or as a light snack throughout the day. Its simplicity reflects the Ligurian culinary philosophy: using a few high-quality, local ingredients to create something extraordinary. The combination of strong flour, water, yeast, salt, and copious amounts of local olive oil is what gives Focaccia Genovese its distinctive texture and flavor. The addition of fresh rosemary isn't just a modern embellishment; it's a classic pairing that enhances the bread's savory depth and aromatic appeal, making Rosemary Focaccia a beloved choice worldwide. It's a bread that tells a story of tradition, ingenuity, and a deep respect for natural flavors.

## Ingredients You'll Need for Rosemary Focaccia

Crafting the perfect Rosemary Focaccia requires a careful selection of ingredients, each playing a crucial role in achieving its authentic taste and texture. Quality is key, especially for the olive oil.

*   **Strong Bread Flour (or All-Purpose Flour + Vital Wheat Gluten):** Around 500g. Bread flour provides the necessary gluten structure for that characteristic airy crumb. If using all-purpose, add 1-2 tablespoons of vital wheat gluten per 500g of flour.
*   **Lukewarm Water:** Approximately 350-400ml. The exact amount can vary based on flour absorption, so start with less and add more if needed. It should be around 35-40°C (95-105°F) to activate the yeast.
*   **Fresh Yeast (or Active Dry/Instant Yeast):** 15g fresh yeast, or 7g (2 ¼ teaspoons) active dry/instant yeast. Fresh yeast offers a slightly richer flavor, but dry yeast works perfectly well.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** At least 80-100ml for the dough, plus a generous amount for the pan and drizzling. This is non-negotiable – use the best quality you can find, as its flavor permeates every part of the bread.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** 10g (about 2 teaspoons) for the dough.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** Two large sprigs, destemmed and roughly chopped, plus extra whole sprigs for garnish.
*   **Coarse Sea Salt (e.g., Maldon or Fleur de Sel):** For sprinkling on top before baking. This provides a delightful textural crunch and burst of salinity.
*   **A Pinch of Sugar (optional):** About ½ teaspoon, to help activate the yeast, especially if using active dry.

## How to Make Authentic Focaccia Genovese: Step-by-Step

Making Focaccia Genovese is a rewarding process that requires patience but relatively little active work.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm water, yeast, and the pinch of sugar (if using). Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. This indicates the yeast is active.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Pour in about 2 tablespoons of the extra virgin olive oil. Using a wooden spoon or your hands, mix until a shaggy, sticky dough forms. Avoid over-mixing; this is a wet dough and doesn't require extensive kneading.
3.  **First Rise (Bulk Fermentation):** Lightly grease another large bowl with olive oil. Transfer the dough to the greased bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
4.  **Prepare the Pan:** Liberally coat a 30x40cm (12x16 inch) baking sheet or a similar-sized pan with a generous amount of extra virgin olive oil – don't be shy! This creates the crispy bottom crust.
5.  **Transfer and Stretch:** Gently deflate the risen dough and carefully transfer it to the prepared baking sheet. Drizzle a little more olive oil over the dough. Using your fingertips, gently press and stretch the dough to fill the pan. If the dough resists, cover it and let it rest for 10-15 minutes before continuing to stretch. You want it to reach the edges of the pan.
6.  **Second Rise (Proofing):** Once the dough fills the pan, cover it again with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise for another 30-45 minutes in a warm place. It should puff up noticeably.
7.  **Dimpling and Topping:** Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). Once the dough has proofed, generously drizzle more extra virgin olive oil over the surface. Then, using your oiled fingertips, gently but firmly press deep dimples all over the dough, ensuring you don't completely deflate it. These dimples are crucial for trapping the olive oil and creating the characteristic texture. Sprinkle the chopped fresh rosemary and the coarse sea salt evenly over the dimpled surface.
8.  **Bake:** Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the Focaccia Genovese is golden brown on top and the bottom is crispy. Keep an eye on it to prevent burning.
9.  **Cool and Serve:** Once baked, immediately transfer the focaccia to a wire rack to cool slightly. Drizzle with a final touch of fresh extra virgin olive oil if desired. Slice and serve warm.

## Expert Tips for the Best Rosemary Focaccia

Achieving the perfect Rosemary Focaccia is an art, but these expert tips will guide you to success:

*   **Quality Olive Oil is Paramount:** We can't stress this enough. A good quality extra virgin olive oil is not just an ingredient; it's a flavor enhancer and a texture creator. It contributes to the focaccia's richness, aroma, and signature crisp bottom.
*   **Don't Over-Knead:** Focaccia Genovese is meant to be a wet, sticky dough. Minimal kneading is sufficient to develop the gluten. Over-kneading can lead to a tough focaccia.
*   **Patience with Rising:** Allow the dough ample time to rise. A slow, steady rise develops better flavor and a more open, airy crumb. Don't rush it.
*   **Generous Dimpling:** The dimples are essential! They create pockets for the olive oil and salt, resulting in those irresistible bursts of flavor and a varied texture. Don't be afraid to press firmly.
*   **Don't Skimp on Toppings:** Fresh rosemary provides an incredible aroma and flavor. Pair it with good quality coarse sea salt for the perfect textural contrast and savory punch.
*   **Preheat Your Pan:** Some bakers like to preheat their baking pan in the oven before adding the dough for an even crispier bottom. If you try this, be extremely careful handling the hot pan.
*   **Serve Warm:** While delicious at any temperature, Rosemary Focaccia is truly at its best when slightly warm, allowing its aromas and textures to shine.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Italian Focaccia

Your freshly baked Rosemary Focaccia is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in numerous ways.

*   **Simply on its Own:** The purest way to appreciate its flavor. Enjoy a piece warm, perhaps with an extra drizzle of good olive oil for dipping.
*   **With Dips and Spreads:** Serve it alongside balsamic vinegar and olive oil, a creamy hummus, or a flavorful tapenade.
*   **As an Appetizer:** A perfect accompaniment to a charcuterie board with cured meats, cheeses, and marinated vegetables.
*   **Alongside Meals:** It’s an excellent companion to hearty soups, fresh salads, or any Italian pasta dish, perfect for soaking up delicious sauces.
*   **For Sandwiches:** Slice the focaccia horizontally and fill it with your favorite ingredients – think prosciutto and mozzarella, grilled vegetables, or even a simple tomato and basil combination. Its soft, airy texture makes for a delightful sandwich bread.
*   **Breakfast Treat:** In true Genovese fashion, enjoy a slice dipped in your morning coffee or milk for a unique start to your day.

## Variations and Substitutions

While Rosemary Focaccia is a classic, don't hesitate to experiment with other flavors and ingredients.

*   **Other Herbs:** Substitute or combine rosemary with fresh thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs for a different aromatic profile.
*   **Vegetable Toppings:** Before baking, press cherry tomatoes (halved or whole), thinly sliced onions, black olives, or roasted garlic cloves into the dimples.
*   **Cheese:** A sprinkle of grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano can be added during the last 5-10 minutes of baking, or even after it comes out of the oven.
*   **Spicy Kick:** A pinch of red pepper flakes can add a subtle heat.
*   **Flour Blends:** While bread flour is ideal, you can experiment with replacing a small portion (up to 20%) with whole wheat flour for a nuttier flavor and denser texture.
*   **Gluten-Free (Advanced):** While challenging to replicate the exact texture, some gluten-free flour blends designed for bread can be used, though the hydration and handling will differ significantly. This would require specific gluten-free recipes.

Baking Focaccia Genovese is more than just following a recipe; it's about embracing a tradition and savoring the simple pleasure of creating something truly delicious from scratch. The combination of fragrant rosemary and rich olive oil transforms this humble flatbread into an unforgettable culinary experience. So, gather your ingredients, get your hands a little sticky, and prepare to fill your home with the intoxicating aroma of authentic Italian baking. Enjoy your journey to Genoa, one glorious bite of Rosemary Focaccia at a time!
